rv.q: I rarely leave the theatre feeling so deeply impacted and, frankly, galvanised by what I've seen.
Williams and Pearson's unflinching direction is most compelling in its bleak brutality.
Nina is raw, honest, dark and menacing. One that is a mesmerising psychological exploration of power, control and manipulative motions that keeps you hooked to the very end.
NINA offers a rich exploration of The Seagull by rewarding those familiar with the original.

The MeToo era has given way to anti-woke posturing, and questions about the way women experience the power of men have become obscured. NINA is a timely return to issues never properly addressed. It is also a powerful and absorbing piece of writing which shakes up expectations.
Its shifts in tone can be disorientating, but its strongest moments are deeply affecting, and the emotional force of its performances lingers beyond the absurdity and uncertainty.
Sometimes through big, grotesque actions, but not always. Acting with and for men often comes with microaggressions and, ultimately, a startling lack of compassion.
